rows.title: A monk, Denver’s mayor and Colorado’s governor discuss AI governance in a rapidly changing tech world
rows.standfirst: At the second annual DenAI Summit, tech and civic leaders gathered to talk about AI tools and what will happen with the state’s AI law

rows.title: US Patent Office is permanently closing its Denver regional hub
rows.standfirst: The closure is not part of the federal shutdown that began Wednesday. The regional office was one of four that opened outside of DC in the past decade to expand the agency’s presence.

rows.title: Xcel asks to skip public hearings to expedite approval of Power Pathways route in Elbert, El Paso counties
rows.standfirst: Colorado utility regulators will consider the request, but it could take up to 250 days to complete the review

rows.title: What’s Working: How Trump’s pick of Fort Collins as new USDA hub could impact Colorado
rows.standfirst: It’s like adding a big new company that must ramp up its workforce, which benefits the local economy. Plus: Colorado businesses feel worse about the end of 2025; furloughed federal workers in the state, and more!

rows.title: In Denver’s Five Points, jazz is the recipe for sparking a comeback on historic Welton Street
rows.standfirst: The neighborhood is battling the reputation that it doesn’t have much to offer with work to preserve the past and focus on defining its own future

rows.title: Government shutdown threatens food aid program relied on by millions of families
rows.standfirst: The shutdown, which began Wednesday, coincided with the beginning of a new fiscal year, meaning programs like WIC, which rely on annual infusions from the federal government, are nearly out of money

rows.title: Colorado just became the first state to cap the price of a prescription drug. What comes next is uncertain.
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Prescription Drug Affordability Board placed what is known as an upper payment limit on the drug Enbrel

rows.title: These 14 Colorado cities aren’t complying with state housing laws. It could cost them $280M in grants.
rows.standfirst: Some of the cities that aren’t in compliance filed a lawsuit against the Polis administration earlier this year over its threat to withhold grant funding if they didn’t comply with the affordable housing initiatives

rows.title: Nederland shopping center that anchored both town and travel burns in early morning fire
rows.standfirst: Most of central Nederland was ordered evacuated early Thursday morning as firefighters worked to protect the Carousel of Happiness, Train Cars Coffee and other local businesses

rows.title: Nederland fire erased a third of local businesses and with it 30% of town sales tax revenue
rows.standfirst: U.S. Rep. Joe Neguse, Gov. Jared Polis visited Caribou Village Shopping Center and promised help navigating access to government help

rows.title: What’s Working: More than 600 federal workers in Colorado filed for unemployment in nine days
rows.standfirst: That includes federal workers who resigned earlier this year but were paid through Sept. 30. Plus: Colorado unemployment numbers increase, why tech companies picked Denver, more!

rows.title: Does Colorado have one of the lowest average property tax rates?
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s 0.5% effective property tax rate was the tenth lowest in the country in 2023, the nonprofit Tax Foundation found

rows.title: Denver’s plan to end tent homelessness with hotel shelters is shrinking again
rows.standfirst: Three hotels repurposed as homeless shelters will stay open, under new management and higher contracts with security

rows.title: Colorado plans to fully digitize paper and analog land records, some dating back to the 1860s, by next year
rows.standfirst: A $2 fee from every property filing since 2016 has helped fund the state’s $21M effort to preserve paper and analog records for digital eternity

rows.title: What’s Working: Robocalls are declining in Colorado but still number in the millions
rows.standfirst: Laws and tech have helped but a CoPIRG analysis found more than 5,000 phone companies aren’t in full compliance. Plus: Behind Comcast’s local layoffs, 1,000+ fed workers unemployed

rows.title: Pushback by counties on solar projects is challenging climate goals, Colorado officials say
rows.standfirst: Cities, counties say report by the Colorado Energy Office was tailored to aid the governor in dictating solar siting rules, much as he has done around housing

rows.title: Manny Rutinel has said a lot about the meat and dairy industries. Now he wants to represent Colorado’s ag capital in Congress.
rows.standfirst: The Democratic state representative’s advocacy in the animal agriculture arena dates back to at least his time as an undergraduate student. He has pushed for a transition to plant-based food.

rows.title: Metro Denver’s average apartment rents fall again, as discounts hit a 15-year high
rows.standfirst: Monthly rents are still higher in the seven-county metro area compared to 2022. They’ve dropped 5% in a year, though the reduction is much more if you count “effective rent”

rows.title: It’s hard to build housing in Littleton. When the council tried to make it easier, residents revolted.
rows.standfirst: After months of acrimony, Littleton voters this November will get a more direct say in city housing policy through city charter amendment 3A and a slate of mayor and council races that have become a referendum on growth.

rows.title: Aging with nowhere to go: Increasing number of people age 65 and older are becoming homeless in Colorado
rows.standfirst: The number of retirement-aged individuals accessing homeless services in metro Denver has increased 15% since 2023. Service providers are struggling to keep up.

rows.title: Colorado ranchers, who have started to increase profits, concerned by Trump proposal to buy cheap Argentine beef
rows.standfirst: While beef prices have increased since COVID — up 51% in five years, according to federal data — the price of cattle has also climbed. That’s allowed Colorado ranchers to reinvest their profits.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado businesses share gloomy forecast — and a bit of optimism
rows.standfirst: A Colorado Business Roundtable survey found 65% of business executives feel negative about state policies but about the same are staying or expanding in the state. Plus: All the latest local economic data we found during the federal shutdown.

rows.title: Duo aiming to harness geothermal power near Mount Princeton sues land board, ex-partners after losing lease
rows.standfirst: It’s the latest salvo in the nearly two-decade long project to build a sustainable power plant south of Buena Vista

rows.title: 3 weeks since Nederland’s town center burned down, displaced businesses are already rebuilding with community’s help
rows.standfirst: GoFundMes have raised $425,000 and neighbors are helping neighbors survive. Several of the fire-affected shop owners are hoping the town sees this as an opportunity to fast track more business development.

rows.title: Telluride owner warns of delay to ski season if Mountain Village leaders raise price of water for snowmaking
rows.standfirst: As communities weigh a lift tax on Telluride ski resort and a tripling of water rates, Chuck Horning blasts “burdens and obstacles” imposed on his company
